one_line_description.value: Netlify is a web hosting and deployment platform for sites and apps, with APIs for deploys, form submissions, JavaScript snippet injection, and DNS management.
one_line_description.quote: Use the Netlify REST API to manage atomic deploys of your sites and apps, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, manage DNS, and so much more.

has_public_api.quote: You can browse the OpenAPI reference for the Netlify API to explore available endpoints.

api_type.quote: Use the Netlify REST API to manage atomic deploys of your sites and apps, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, manage DNS, and so much more.

api_breadth.value: REST, broad read-write surface spanning sites/projects, deploys, form submissions, DNS, snippet injection and more; no endpoint count appears in the fetched pages
api_breadth.quote: Learn how to integrate with Netlify's REST API to programmatically manage your projects, deploys, and more.

docs_url.quote: This document covers the basics for interacting with the Netlify API, plus instructions for deploying sites and notes on some commonly used endpoints.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: You'll need an application client key and a client secret to integrate with the Netlify API.

access_model.quote: You can register a new application in your Netlify user settings for OAuth applications.

access_notes.value: No sales contact or app review gates the core REST API: a free plan exists (300 credits/month) and developers self-generate personal access tokens or register OAuth apps in user settings. Enterprise-only features (e.g., organization webhooks per search snippets) require an Enterprise plan.
access_notes.quote: Netlify's Credit-based plans currently include the Free plan, Personal plan, and Pro plan.

rate_limits.quote: To protect Netlify from getting flooded by automated deploys or misbehaving applications, the Netlify API is rate limited.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Versioned base path https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/; backward-incompatible changes bump the version marker while old URLs remain supported; the REST API follows semantic versioning per the release-phases documentation.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: If we change the API in backward-incompatible ways, we'll bump the version marker and maintain stable support for the old URLs.

verdict_reason: Netlify publishes a broad REST API (v1 base URL with an OpenAPI reference) covering sites, deploys, forms, DNS and more. Credentials are fully self-serve: a free plan exists and developers can generate personal access tokens or register OAuth2 applications from user settings, with no sales contact or app review required. Only certain add-on features (e.g., organization webhooks) are Enterprise-gated.
open_questions: Official rate-limit numbers are not in the fetched pages; a forum snippet mentions 500 requests/minute for paid accounts but was not part of the evidence bundle.
OAuth scopes/permissions are not described in the fetched pages; the implicit-grant example uses client_id, response_type, redirect_uri and state only.

Webhooks: search snippets referenced organization webhooks and deploy notifications, but those pages were not fetched into SOURCES, so webhook support is unconfirmed from the evidence (organization webhooks appear to be Enterprise-only).
No documented dedicated API sandbox/test environment was found in the fetched pages; deploy previews/branch deploys were mentioned only in snippets (pricing page, blog), which were not fetched.

SDK languages: the docs mention 'two API clients for your convenience' but the text is truncated and no language names appear in the evidence; the developers.netlify.com/sdk page describes an extension SDK, not API client libraries.
Endpoint/resource count for the REST API is not stated in the fetched pages (only that an OpenAPI reference exists).
No community/third-party MCP server URLs appeared in the evidence.
